newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes higher despite Iraq tension.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes higher despite Iraq tension.

text.p: Inflows of foreign equity funds pulled the Taiwan dollar a firmer close on Wednesday but dealers said the U.S. dollar's strength overseas over tensions in the Gulf gave the local unit only limited room to rise.
The local unit finished at T$27.494 against Tuesday's T$27.516. Turnover was US$226.5 million.
"As the situation in the Gulf did not change significantly since yesterday, foreign fund inflows were the main factor affecting the market today," said one dealer.
Foreign funds started to flow in after Morgan Stanley added Taiwan to its global indices on September 2, dealers said.
"Foreign funds won't continue to come in because the domestic economy is not that good," the dealer said. "Further Taiwan dollar appreciation should be limited."
Since May, the government has been trying to nudge the Taiwan dollar lower to spur exports, the island's lifeblood.

Fresh development in the Gulf should still guide the overall market but since many overseas markets had started to shrug off the impact of the second U.S. missile attack on Iraq, dealers did not expect major movements in the domestic market.
A T$27.47-52 trading range was seen for Thursday.
